blocks.explanation:
Unit place digit (ikaai ka hindsa) kisi number ka sab se aakhri digit hota hai. \((25)^{315}\) itna bara number hai ke isay poora likhna mumkin hi nahi, is liye hum shortcut dhoondte hain.
Diya kya hai? \((25)^{315}\). Find kya karna hai? Sirf aakhri digit.
Rule kaunsa? Binomial theorem: base ko (10 ka multiple) + (aakhri digit) likh kar expand karein to pata chalta hai ke aakhri digit sirf base ke aakhri digit par depend karta hai.
Plan: 25 = 20 + 5, expand, 0 par khatam hone wale terms chhor dein, phir 5 ki powers ka pattern dekhein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((25)^{315}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka unit place digit.
Tareeqa: Base ko (10 ka koi multiple) + (us ka aakhri digit) mein torenge aur binomial theorem se expand karenge. Jis term mein 10 ka multiple hoga woh 0 par khatam hoga, aur 0 wala number jama karne se aakhri digit nahi badalta. Yun poora sawal ek chhoti si power par aa jata hai.

Base ko do hisson mein torein
\[(25)^{315} = (20 + 5)^{315}\]
Kyun: 20 ko 10 se poora divide kiya ja sakta hai, aur 5 hi 25 ka aakhri digit hai. Hum chahte hain ke ek hissa '0 par khatam' ho aur doosra hissa chhota sa digit ho, kyunke sara khel isi chhote digit ka hai.

Binomial theorem se expand karein
\[(20 + 5)^{315} = 20^{315}\]
\[+ {}^{315}C_{1}\,20^{314}\cdot 5 + \dots\]
\[+ {}^{315}C_{314}\,20\cdot 5^{314} + 5^{315}\]
Kyun: Formula \((a + x)^n = a^n + {}^nC_1 a^{n-1}x + \dots + x^n\) mein \(a = 20\), \(x = 5\), \(n = 315\) rakha. Ghaur se dekhiye: aakhri term \(5^{315}\) ke ilawa har term mein kam az kam ek dafa 20 zaroor aata hai. Poori expansion likhne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf yeh pattern samajhna kaafi hai.

0 par khatam hone wale terms hata dein
\[(25)^{315} = 10k + 5^{315}\]
Kyun: Jis number mein 20 ka factor ho woh 10 ka multiple hai, yani us ka aakhri digit 0 hai. Aise sab terms ko jama kar ke \(10k\) likh diya. Ab socho: kisi number mein 10, 20, 1000 jama karne se us ka aakhri digit badalta hai? Nahi. Is liye unit digit sirf \(5^{315}\) se tay hoga.
Dhyan dein: Yeh \(10k\) wala hissa bohat bara hai, lekin aakhri digit ke liye bilkul be-asar hai; size se ghabrayein nahi.

5 ki powers ka aakhri digit
\[5^1 = 5,\quad 5^2 = 25\]
\[5^3 = 125,\quad 5^4 = 625\]
Kyun: Jo number 5 par khatam ho, usay 5 se multiply karein to naya aakhri digit \(5 \times 5 = 25\) ka aakhri digit hota hai, yani phir 5. Yeh silsila kabhi nahi tootta, is liye 5 ki har power 5 par hi khatam hoti hai, chahe power 315 ho ya 3 lakh.

Tasdeeq
\[25^2 = 625,\quad 25^3 = 15625\]
Kyun: 25 ki chhoti powers khud hisaab kar ke dekh lein, dono 5 par khatam ho rahi hain, bilkul jaise humare tareeqe ne bataya tha. Kitab ki Example 24(ii) mein bhi yehi baat use hui hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\((25)^{315}\) ka unit place digit \(5\) hai.
Yaad rakhiye: 5 (ya 6, 0, 1) par khatam hone wale number ki har power ka aakhri digit wohi rehta hai.

blocks.explanation:
Pichle part ki tarah yahan bhi sirf base ka aakhri digit, yani 4, faisla karega.
Lekin 4 ki powers kabhi 4 par khatam hoti hain aur kabhi 6 par, is liye humein dekhna hai ke 45 wali power kis taraf jati hai.
Rule kaunsa? Binomial theorem do dafa: pehle 74 = 70 + 4, phir 16 = 10 + 6.
Plan: \(4^{45}\) tak pohanchein, usay \(4 \cdot 16^{22}\) likhein, aur 16 ki power ka aakhri digit dekhein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((74)^{45}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka unit place digit.
Tareeqa: \(74 = 70 + 4\) likhne se expansion ke baad sirf \(4^{45}\) aakhri digit par asar daalta hai. Phir \(4^{45}\) ko 16 ki power mein badlenge, kyunke 16 ka aakhri digit 6 hai aur 6 ki har power 6 par khatam hoti hai, jis se kaam bohat aasaan ho jata hai.

Aakhri digit ki power tak pohanchein
\[(74)^{45} = (70 + 4)^{45}\]
\[= 10k + 4^{45}\]
Kyun: Expansion mein \(4^{45}\) ke ilawa har term mein 70 ka factor hai, aur 70 ka multiple hamesha 0 par khatam hota hai. To woh sab terms milkar \(10k\) ban gaye, jo aakhri digit nahi badalte.

Power ko 16 ki madad se likhein
\[4^{45} = 4 \cdot 4^{44}\]
\[= 4 \cdot (4^2)^{22} = 4 \cdot 16^{22}\]
Kyun: 45 odd hai, is liye pehle ek 4 alag kar diya: \(45 = 1 + 44\). Phir \(44 = 2 \times 22\), aur laws of indices \(a^{m+n} = a^m a^n\) aur \(a^{mn} = (a^m)^n\) se \(4^{44} = (4^2)^{22} = 16^{22}\) bana. Maqsad yeh tha ke koi aisa base mil jaye jis ka aakhri digit power lene se na badle.

\(16^{22}\) ka aakhri digit
\[16^{22} = (10 + 6)^{22}\]
\[= 10h + 6^{22}\]
Kyun: Wohi purani chaal: 10 wale sab terms 0 par khatam, sirf \(6^{22}\) bacha. Ab \(6 \times 6 = 36\) ka aakhri digit phir 6 hai, is liye 6 ki har power 6 par khatam hoti hai (6, 36, 216, 1296, ...). Matlab \(16^{22}\) ka aakhri digit 6 hai.

4 se multiply karein
\[4 \times 6 = 24\]
Kyun: \(4^{45} = 4 \times (\text{6 par khatam hone wala number})\). Do numbers ke product ka aakhri digit sirf un ke aakhri digits ke product se aata hai: \(4 \times 6 = 24\), yani aakhri digit 4.
Dhyan dein: 24 poora jawab nahi; unit place digit sirf ek digit hota hai, yani 4.

Tasdeeq
\[4^1 = 4,\ 4^2 = 16,\ 4^3 = 64,\ 4^4 = 256\]
Kyun: 4 ki powers ke aakhri digits 4, 6, 4, 6 ... baari baari aate hain: odd power par 4, even power par 6. 45 odd hai, to jawab 4 hona chahiye, aur humara jawab bhi 4 hai. Do alag raaston se ek hi jawab aaye to yaqeen pakka ho jata hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\((74)^{45}\) ka unit place digit \(4\) hai.
Yaad rakhiye: 4 ki odd power ka aakhri digit 4 aur even power ka 6 hota hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan base ka aakhri digit 3 hai, to humein \(3^{87}\) ka aakhri digit chahiye.
3 ki powers ka aakhri digit ek jaisa nahi rehta (3, 9, 7, 1 ...), is liye hum \(3^4 = 81\) ki madad lenge, jo 1 par khatam hota hai.
Rule kaunsa? Binomial theorem, pehle 573 = 570 + 3 aur phir 81 = 80 + 1.
Plan: \(3^{87}\) tak aayein, 81 ki power alag karein, aur phir bacha hua hissa multiply karein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((573)^{87}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka unit place digit.
Tareeqa: \(573 = 570 + 3\) likhne se sirf \(3^{87}\) aakhri digit par asar daalta hai. \(3^4 = 81\) ka aakhri digit 1 hai, aur 1 par khatam hone wale number ki har power bhi 1 par khatam hoti hai. Is liye 87 mein se 4 ke jitne poore blocks nikal sakein, woh sab 1 ban jayenge.

Aakhri digit ki power tak pohanchein
\[(573)^{87} = (570 + 3)^{87}\]
\[= 10k + 3^{87}\]
Kyun: \(3^{87}\) ke ilawa har term mein 570 ka factor hai, jo 10 ka multiple hai. Yeh sab terms 0 par khatam hote hain aur aakhri digit ko nahi chherte.

Power ko 4 ke blocks mein torein
\[87 = 4 \times 21 + 3\]
\[3^{87} = 3^{3}\cdot (3^4)^{21}\]
\[= 27 \cdot 81^{21}\]
Kyun: 87 ko 4 se divide kiya: quotient 21, remainder 3. To \(3^{87}\) mein 4-4 ke 21 block hain aur 3 power bach jati hai. Har block \(3^4 = 81\) hai, is liye \((3^4)^{21} = 81^{21}\).

\(81^{21}\) ka aakhri digit
\[81^{21} = (80 + 1)^{21}\]
\[= 10h + 1^{21} = 10h + 1\]
Kyun: Expansion mein aakhri term ke ilawa har term mein 80 hai, jo 0 par khatam hota hai. Aakhri term \(1^{21} = 1\) hai, kyunke 1 ko kitni dafa bhi multiply karein, 1 hi rehta hai. Is liye \(81^{21}\) ka aakhri digit 1 hai.

27 se multiply karein
\[27 \times (10h + 1) = 270h + 27\]
Kyun: \(270h\) 0 par khatam hota hai, to aakhri digit sirf 27 ka aakhri digit hai, yani 7.
Dhyan dein: Remainder 3 ko bhool kar sirf \(81^{21}\) dekh lena aam ghalti hai; tab jawab 1 aa jata hai jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq
\[3^1 = 3,\ 3^2 = 9,\ 3^3 = 27,\ 3^4 = 81\]
Kyun: 3 ki powers ke aakhri digits 3, 9, 7, 1 ka chakkar lagate hain, jis ki lambai 4 hai. \(87 = 4 \times 21 + 3\), yani 21 poore chakkar ke baad chakkar ka teesra digit aata hai, jo 7 hai. Kitab ki Example 24 bhi yehi remainder wala tareeqa use karti hai, aur jawab wohi 7 hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\((573)^{87}\) ka unit place digit \(7\) hai.
Yaad rakhiye: 3 ki powers ke aakhri digits ka chakkar 3, 9, 7, 1 hai.
